idea.rawIdea: A shared online inventory for independent bookshops, so a customer can search once and reserve a book at the nearest indie shop that has it in stock instead of ordering from Amazon.
idea.problem: Readers who want to buy from independent shops can't tell which nearby shop has a book, so they default to next-day delivery from a giant retailer.
idea.targetUser: Urban readers aged 25–45 who already feel guilty buying books online and would walk 15 minutes to support a local shop.
idea.context: Independent bookshops each run separate point-of-sale systems with no shared discovery layer; many already export stock feeds nightly.
constraints: Shops will not pay an upfront fee
Must work with existing point-of-sale exports
assumptions: Readers will accept same-day pickup instead of delivery
openQuestions: Do shops want to be compared to each other on one map?

questions.question: Is the first customer the reader or the bookshop owner?
questions.whyItMatters: It decides whose language the brand speaks and who the hero of the story is.

questions.question: What should a reader feel at the moment they pick up the reserved book?
questions.whyItMatters: That feeling is the emotional payoff every piece of copy points toward.

questions.question: Is taking on Amazon part of the story, or something you'd avoid saying out loud?
questions.whyItMatters: An explicit enemy sharpens the positioning but narrows the tone.

answers.q1: Readers. Shops sign up once readers show demand.
answers.q2: Like a bookseller put it aside for them personally.
answers.q3: Never name Amazon. We're for something, not against someone.

directions.label: The Neighbourhood Hold
directions.positioning: For city readers who'd rather walk to a shop than wait for a courier, the fastest way to find a book on a real shelf nearby.
directions.differentiator: Live stock from real shops, with a named bookseller holding your copy.
directions.valueProp: Search once, pick it up today, and keep your local shop alive.

traits.name: Neighbourly
traits.justification: The product only works within walking distance.

traits.name: Quick
traits.justification: It competes with next-day delivery on speed of certainty.

traits.name: Warm
traits.justification: Readers told us the payoff is feeling personally looked after.

directions.label: The Bookseller's Ally
directions.positioning: The quiet ally behind independent bookshops, giving them the reach of a chain without losing what makes them independent.
directions.differentiator: Built around booksellers' judgement, not an algorithm.
directions.valueProp: Every shop's shelves, one search, still personal.

traits.name: Loyal
traits.justification: The archetype is the ally who never takes the spotlight.

traits.name: Knowledgeable
traits.justification: Booksellers' expertise is the asset being amplified.

traits.name: Understated
traits.justification: The shops are the stars; the network stays in the background.

directions.label: Mischief on the Shelves
directions.positioning: A cheeky treasure map of your city's bookshops for readers who like the hunt as much as the book.
directions.differentiator: Turns finding a book into a small local adventure.
directions.valueProp: Your next book is closer than you think. Go get it.

traits.name: Playful
traits.justification: The tone axis pushes hard away from worthy bookishness.

traits.name: Curious
traits.justification: Rewards readers who browse and wander.

traits.name: Bold
traits.justification: It needs to stand out against polite literary brands.

critiques.strongestPoint: I instantly get it: find it nearby, grab it today.
objections: What if the shop sells my copy before I get there?

critiques.strongestPoint: Speed of certainty is a real edge over delivery.
objections: Depends on stock data being accurate
Walking distance limits the market to dense cities

critiques.strongestPoint: The personal 'held for you' detail is specific.
I like that booksellers stay in charge.
objections: It sounds like it's for shop owners, not me

critiques.strongestPoint: Most credible story for signing up shops.
objections: Readers are the stated first customer, and this speaks to shops
'Reach of a chain' is a stock B2B phrase

critiques.strongestPoint: Makes me want to go on a book hunt this weekend.
objections: Sometimes I just need the book, not an adventure
Playfulness may undercut trust in reservations

critiques.strongestPoint: No one else in books sounds like this.
objections: 'Treasure map' metaphor could get cute fast

names.name: Nearshelf
names.rationale: Says exactly what it does: the nearest shelf with your book.

names.name: Holdfast
names.rationale: A copy held fast for you; also suggests loyalty.

names.name: Spinewalk
names.rationale: Book spines plus the walk to the shop.

tagline.text: Your book, on a shelf nearby.

verbal.oneLiner: Nearshelf searches the independent bookshops around you and has a bookseller hold your copy for same-day pickup.

messageHierarchy.primary: The book you want is probably ten minutes away.
supporting: Live stock from real independent shops
A named bookseller holds it for 24 hours
Pick it up today, no delivery wait

principles: Talk like a neighbour, not a platform
Be specific about time and distance
do: Name the shop and the bookseller
samples: Mira at Paper Lantern is holding your copy until 6pm tomorrow.
Three shops within a 12-minute walk have it.

visual.shapeLanguage: Soft-cornered rectangles like book spines; a single map-pin notch as the recurring motif.
visual.imageryStyle: Warm, daylight photos of real shop interiors and hands on books; no stock people smiling at phones.
visual.logoBrief: A wordmark in DM Serif Display with the 'h' ascender drawn as a book spine leaning on its neighbour.
avoid: Library clichés like owls and glasses

violations.fix: Replace with a concrete, specific claim.

revisions.reason: Guardian revise pass removed the cliché and matched the quick, neighbourly voice.

launch.heroHeadline: The book you want is ten minutes away.
launch.heroSub: Nearshelf checks the independent shops around you and has a bookseller hold your copy for pickup today.
launch.pitch: Readers want to buy from independent bookshops but can't see what's on their shelves, so they order online. Nearshelf joins up the stock of local shops into one search and turns a reservation into a same-day pickup with a named bookseller holding the copy.

socialPosts.text: Searched for a book. Three shops within a 12-minute walk had it. Mira at Paper Lantern is holding it until 6. That's Nearshelf.
Independent bookshops don't lack books; they lack being findable. Nearshelf puts their live stock into one search and turns it into same-day pickups.
Your book, on a shelf nearby. Found it, held it, go get it.

trail.reason: Structured the raw idea into problem, user and constraints.
Asked about the first customer, the payoff moment and the competitor stance.
Split on audience wedge, archetype and tone so the three options differ in kind.
Three critics scored each direction; A led on audience fit and clarity.
Nearshelf is literal about distance and scored as Distinct (41).
Neighbourly, quick and warm traits became voice principles; competitors never named.
dmserif-dmsans is tagged warm and approachable, matching the traits.
Book-cloth greens and reds; avoided map-app blue.
Caught one cliché in a voice sample and rewrote it; no cross-field violations remained.
Hero uses the primary message with a concrete time; posts follow the voice samples.
